evidence_register.title: MRBTP: Efficient Multi-Robot Behavior Tree Planning and Collaboration
paper_supported: The paper describes decentralized multi-robot behavior-tree planning with shared symbolic goals and per-agent action models.
The paper claims soundness and completeness for its stated formulation and reports warehouse and everyday-service evaluations.
not_established_here: Applicability to SO-101, MuJoCo, current cameras, real hardware, or this project's protocols.

evidence_register.runtime_and_task: Python >=3.9; self-contained MiniGrid multi-robot behavior-tree tutorial; its documented smoke task uses two robots in a DoorKey-style grid world.
evidence_register.metrics_or_execution_note: The README documents stochastic execution and an approximately 70% single smoke-run success statement, with a verifier that retries five times; this has not been independently executed in this project.
limitations: 2-D symbolic/grid simulation is not a MuJoCo manipulation model.
Repository-demo behavior is not reproduction in this project.

evidence_register.runtime_and_task: Python 3.10 declared by README; MiniGrid/BabyAI demos and optional VirtualHome household scenario; repository documents a two-agent DoorKey 8x8 example.
evidence_register.metrics_or_execution_note: No upstream numeric result has been re-executed or adopted by this project.
limitations: VirtualHome binary is optional and the README says Windows is the fully tested platform for that scenario.
No SO-101/camera compatibility claim is made by this record.

evidence_register.title: RoCo: Dialectic Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models
paper_supported: RoCo introduces six tabletop multi-robot manipulation tasks (RoCoBench) plus a text dataset.
Its described pipeline uses inter-robot LLM dialogue, task-space waypoint proposals, collision feedback, and centralized multi-arm motion planning.
The project page describes a real-world demonstration with one robot and a human, and identifies OWL-ViT object-detection errors as a primary bottleneck.
not_established_here: That dialogue improves the current system, that its outcomes transfer to SO-101, or that it is safe to use an LLM for controls.

evidence_register.runtime_and_task: Paired code repository for RoCo/RoCoBench; project material describes six MuJoCo tabletop collaborative-manipulation tasks.
evidence_register.metrics_or_execution_note: Task success, semantic adaptation, and RoCoBench-Text are described upstream; this project has not cloned, installed, or run the repository.
limitations: The benchmark requires multiple manipulation agents and its motion-planning stack; it is not a current one-SO-101 baseline.

evidence_register.title: Partially Observable Task and Motion Planning with Uncertainty and Risk Awareness
paper_supported: TAMPURA addresses initial-state and action-outcome uncertainty, including information gathering and undesirable/irreversible outcomes.
The paper reports comparisons to determinized planning, direct search, and reinforcement learning in its stated robotics problems, including two real-world problems.
not_established_here: A TAMPURA abstraction/controller can be instantiated for SO-101, or that its reported comparisons reproduce under this project's setup.

candidate_simulation_assets.upstream_requirements: The asset README states MuJoCo 3.1.3 or later and documents a camera mount.
limitations: The upstream model is a public robot description, not evidence that it matches this specific physical SO-101 calibration.
It does not provide this project's two fixed-depth-camera intrinsics, extrinsics, synchronization, noise, or actual coverage.
Third-party simulation environment; no equivalence to project hardware or camera setup has been checked.
